limits.summary: Abort mode without js-cleanup (gate-a, sizez-a with js-cleanup=off): destructors do not run on a host exception; by design (CONTRACT: js-cleanup=on is opt-in). Host-throw probes compared only in unwind configs and relz-a.

Rust panics never unwind in either mode (CONTRACT: a Rust panic is still an abort), so drop-on-panic ordering is not comparable to native panic=unwind; probes keep drop observers away from Rust panics.
Panic messages are not formatted by the probe panic handler (no_std); only file/line/column are compared.

compile_core.sh forces -Coverflow-checks=off -Cdebug-assertions=off in every profile, so arithmetic-overflow panics inside #[track_caller] fns cannot occur; only div/rem-by-zero and i32::MIN/-1 were tested (native oracle compiled with the same flags).

Custom #[global_allocator] not tested: needs an unsafe GlobalAlloc impl with no backing allocator in no_std; allocator_api Arena shapes not probed. Allocation inside flattened-&mut callees was tested with the default allocator (uw_alloc_throw).

Sysroot RawParts/byte_slice_ref peeling is reachable from safe code only through sysroot bodies (Vec::as_slice, split_at, chunks_exact, str::as_bytes); slice::from_raw_parts and user extern imports named like runtime members are unsafe and were not used as verdict evidence.
js-modules=esm, the JSC engine (except inside the committed r3 scripts), and timing were not measured.
Unwind-mode host-throw oracle is native aarch64 (usize=64); unwind probes avoid usize-width-dependent arithmetic. All other probes use a native wasm32 LLVM build (usize=32).

preExisting.summary: JSC_PANIC=abort with js-opt=on and no MIR inline (gate-a) and release-size+inline-z abort (sizez-a): a failed bounds-check/arith assert throws `rust abort: index out of bounds` WITHOUT running the #[panic_handler] (its location output is lost). Identical output on base.

JSC_RUST_MIR_INLINE=on JSC_RUST_OPT_LEVEL=z in unwind mode (relz-u, latz-u) and sizez-a: #[track_caller] location of slice index/range panics reports core/src/slice/index.rs:414:13 instead of the caller; identical on base. relz-a (abort) is correct. Also the committed Round-3 fixture 332_r3_assert_tc_panic.rs: under relz-u/latz-u/sizez-a it reports 28:5 / 33:5 (inside div_tc/idx_tc) instead of 43/49/54:5 for modes 0/1/2 on BOTH candidate and base (base compiles the same source identically), so 332 fails the suite in relz-u for a pre-existing reason; gate-u, rel-u, relz-a are correct on both.

A #[track_caller] fn reified to a fn pointer (`let g: fn() -> &Location = here; g()`) crashes with TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading filename) in every config; native prints the definition location. Identical on base.

String::make_ascii_uppercase() (write through &mut str) is silently lost: prints original lowercase text and hash. Identical on base; CONTRACT.md documents that a write through &mut str is lost, but it is a silent wrong answer in safe Rust.
js-cleanup=on (release-balanced abort, relz-a): when a Vec element destructor throws (host exception), the remaining elements are not dropped (native drops them during unwinding). Identical on base.
closure passed to generic FnMut under inline-z in unwind mode is refused at compile time: requires semantic cleanup lowering ... SpreadNotTuple (fail-closed refusal). Identical on base.

iter_mut()/iter() over a mutable empty array `let mut e: [u8; 0] = []` passed as &mut [u8] aborts with `rustc_codegen_js: ptr_eq on a pointer that was offset from an address with no provenance` (fail-loud refusal at run time) in all 9 configs; identical on base
